summary: Twelve comment-endorsed tools, books, furniture, and media picks from 30 fully crawled HN threads.
telegram_footer: 12 items surfaced | 30/30 current front-page stories processed | history + run artifact updated.

items.name: git-arr
items.summary: A small Git repository browser that can generate static HTML.
items.why_included: A commenter reported using it successfully as an alternative repository front end.
items.evidence: The commenter said they had been using git-arr with some success.

evidence_sources.author: singpolyma3
evidence_sources.excerpt: I've been using git-arr instead with some success

items.name: smolvm
items.source_story_title: Omarchy: Any User Process Can Escalate to Root
items.summary: A portable microVM engine for isolated local workloads and coding agents.
items.why_included: A user praised smol machines for Docker-socket and Docker-in-Docker workloads.
items.evidence: The commenter called smolmachines wonderful and said they use it for Docker socket and nested-Docker workloads.

evidence_sources.author: K0IN
evidence_sources.excerpt: smolmachines is a wonderful program to solve this, I use this mostly for stuff needing docker socket / docker in docker

items.name: docstr
items.summary: A Rust macro crate for ergonomic multiline string literals.
items.why_included: A Rust user adopted it to recover a multiline-string style they missed from Zig.
items.evidence: The commenter said they started using docstr and prefer its style for long text.

evidence_sources.author: Rendello
evidence_sources.excerpt: I've started using the Rust macro library `docstr` [1], which does the same thing

items.name: Amp Orbs
items.summary: Remote machines where Amp coding agents run independently of your computer.
items.why_included: A paying user strongly praised the workflow, integrations, and ease of use.
items.evidence: The commenter called Orbs fantastic, praised its surrounding features, and described it as their best $20 monthly developer-tool spend.

evidence_sources.author: altschuler
evidence_sources.excerpt: I've found Orbs to be just fantastic! The "it's just a VM, everybody has that" argument misses the point, the real value lies in just how easy it is to use and the surrounding functionality.

items.name: Storyteller
items.summary: A self-hosted platform that aligns ebooks and audiobooks for immersive reading.
items.why_included: A user praised its cross-device position syncing between listening and e-ink reading.
items.evidence: The commenter said Storyteller works great and syncs reading position across devices.

evidence_sources.author: tcoff91
evidence_sources.excerpt: Storyteller works great for this. It even syncs your position across devices.

items.name: Don't Make Me Think
items.summary: Steve Krug's concise guide to intuitive web and interface usability.
items.why_included: A commenter gave the UX classic a direct, unqualified endorsement.
items.evidence: The commenter said they love the UX-design book.

evidence_sources.author: mcbishop
evidence_sources.excerpt: I love the UX-design book: Don't Make Me Think.

items.name: The Art of Action
items.source_story_title: Coordination Headwind: How Organizations Are Like Slime Molds
items.summary: Stephen Bungay's guide to closing gaps between plans, actions, and results.
items.why_included: A commenter explicitly recommended it for loosely coupled, highly aligned teams.
items.evidence: The commenter recommended the book and tied its central idea to aligned, loosely coupled teams.

evidence_sources.author: jodacola
evidence_sources.excerpt: I recommend reading The Art of Action by Stephen Bungay on this particular topic. A line in this presentation about loosely coupled, highly aligned teams is a major idea straight out of this book.

items.name: Corps Business
items.source_story_title: Coordination Headwind: How Organizations Are Like Slime Molds
items.summary: A book on decentralized decision-making and management principles from the U.S. Marines.
items.why_included: A reader recommended it for understanding mission-led, decentralized organizations.
items.evidence: The commenter called reading it their best answer for building such organizations, while noting dated sections.

evidence_sources.author: alexpotato
evidence_sources.excerpt: my best answer is just to read the book. NOTE: the book was written in the late 1990s so there are some parts that are dated but the overall concepts are still sound.

items.name: IKEA KALLAX
items.summary: A modular cube-shelving range for books, boxes, and general storage.
items.why_included: A long-term user strongly praised its durability, versatility, capacity, and price.
items.evidence: The commenter described KALLAX as sturdy, versatile, durable, and well priced across several uses.

evidence_sources.author: sheepscreek
evidence_sources.excerpt: I love KALLAX the most of all IKEA series. Sturdy as heck, can take a lot of weight, extremely versatile and durable.

items.name: Thuma bed frames
items.summary: Japanese-joinery bed frames designed for tool-free assembly and easier moving.
items.why_included: An owner strongly praised their moving convenience and build quality.
items.evidence: The commenter said their Thuma frames are amazing for moving and very high quality.

evidence_sources.author: nunez
evidence_sources.excerpt: We use Thuma Japanese joinery bed frames, which are AMAZING for moving and very high quality

items.name: Qubes OS
items.source_story_title: Arbitrary code execution in QubesOS via copy-to-VM error reporting backchannel
items.summary: A security-focused desktop OS that isolates activities in virtualized compartments.
items.why_included: A user still trusts it for a dedicated financial laptop despite a graphics limitation.
items.evidence: The commenter remains impressed and uses Qubes OS for financial tasks, while noting the lack of graphics acceleration.

evidence_sources.author: zby
evidence_sources.excerpt: I am still impressed by QubesOS track and I use it for my dedicated 'financials' laptop. IMHO the thing that is holding back QubesOS is the lack of hardware acceleration for graphics

items.name: Everything You Need To Know About NASA's Roman Space Telescope
items.summary: A NASA video explaining Roman's scale, mission, and place alongside other telescopes.
items.why_included: A commenter specifically praised the video's sense of scale.
items.evidence: The commenter called the video quite good at conveying the undertaking's scale.

evidence_sources.author: stuart78
evidence_sources.excerpt: This video linked from the site is quite good at adding a sense of scale to the undertaking.
